title: Deployment metadata checksum drift caused rollout to stall and blocked automated failover
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During a staged model rollout, a mismatch between deployment metadata checksums in the control plane and serving nodes caused the rollout controller to refuse traffic updates. The mismatch blocked the automated failover/rollback path for ~37 minutes and caused elevated latency for a subset of customers using dedicated capacity pools.
incident_summary: At 2026-03-01 09:12 UTC a gradual rollout of model v13 -> v14 exceeded our canary policy. The rollout controller attempted to apply new traffic weights but the route translator rejected updates because serving nodes reported a different deployment metadata checksum than the control plane expected. The controller entered a retry loop and did not trigger the automated failover policy because the checksum mismatch prevented the condition evaluation that flips the failover gate. Traffic to affected routes oscillated and tail latency spiked for ~37 minutes until a manual reconciliation was performed.
timeline: 2026-03-01 09:12 UTC - Rollout started. 2026-03-01 09:18 UTC - First weight update failed with checksum mismatch on 3/12 serving nodes. 2026-03-01 09:22 UTC - Controller retried repeatedly; alerting threshold (latency) fired. 2026-03-01 09:28 UTC - Ops paged on-call. 2026-03-01 09:37 UTC - Investigation identified metadata checksum divergence after a control-plane migration earlier that morning. 2026-03-01 09:49 UTC - Manual reconciliation pushed (re-sync metadata and bump epoch); rollout resumed. 2026-03-01 09:50 UTC - Traffic returned to expected distribution. Total customer impact window ~37m.
root_cause: A metadata serialization change deployed as part of an unrelated control-plane migration produced a different ordering of non-functional fields. Serving nodes calculated a checksum from serialized metadata and the controller compared against the pre-migration checksum. The checksum comparison is too strict and lacks a tolerant reconciliation path; combined with lack of a reconciliation job and an overly conservative failover gate, automated recovery did not run.
mitigations_taken: 1) Rolled back the control-plane migration on the metadata path where safe. 2) Performed manual metadata reconciliation by forcing a metadata resync and epoch bump on affected serving nodes. 3) Temporarily relaxed checksum strictness in controller to allow weight updates if semantic equality verified. 4) Added ad-hoc alerting for checksum divergence across region clusters.
action_items: ENG-140322: Implement a deterministic canonical serializer for deployment metadata (remove non-deterministic field ordering) - owner: Marco Li - estimate: 8
ENG-140323: Add a reconciliation controller job that periodically compares control-plane and serving metadata checksums and auto-resyncs minor divergences - owner: Priya Nair - estimate: 5
ENG-140324: Introduce a semantic-equality check that falls back to field-level comparison before blocking rollouts - owner: Ricardo Gomez - estimate: 5
ENG-140325: Update rollout runbook to include checksum-divergence play and one-click resync tooling - owner: SRE Team - estimate: 3
ENG-140326: Add e2e test covering control-plane migration + rollout to catch serialization changes in CI - owner: QA - estimate: 3
ENG-140327: Improve monitoring and alerts: metric for % of nodes with checksum mismatch and a paging threshold - owner: Observability - estimate: 2
ENG-140328: Review and harden automated failover gates so they can operate on semantic equality signals, not only raw checksum boolean - owner: Platform - estimate: 4
owner_notes: We prioritized quick manual remediation to restore traffic; the long-term fix is a deterministic serializer and a reconciliation loop. There is a trade-off between strict checksum enforcement (fast rejection of incompatible changes) and availability during benign serialization changes. The design direction recommended by the incident owners is to preserve strictness for major schema changes (major version bump) but accept semantic-equality for patch-level reorders.
